author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected after booking: its date and description change in place, under the same validation as booking, and the pet does not gain a second visit.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction is started, then that visit's current date and description are offered for change
given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are supplied, then that visit carries the new values and the owner's record is shown
given a pet with one booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet still has exactly one visit
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused and the date is named
given a visit whose date has already passed, when it is corrected, then a date later than today is still required (Visits edge case 3)
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, still declined)
a visible way into the correction from the owner's record - the owner deferred it to a possible follow-up request
refusing a correction whose visit belongs to a different pet or owner - recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md, not specified here
notes: Owner constraints quoted at intake-decision line 2, decisions 4 and 5: the address is GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, reusing the existing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template and its `visit` model attribute, redirecting to the owner detail page on success and redisplaying the form on failure. NG-5 narrowing recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-06-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowed.md and amended onto the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR. Two open product questions recorded in docs/prd.md rather than escalated, per the owner's standing instruction to take the narrowest reading and record the open question. No prd-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope, but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction is a second route pair on the existing VisitController, inside the owner feature package (system-design.md#package-structure), reusing pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm unchanged. One adjustment makes it minor rather than covered: the controller's shared @ModelAttribute("visit") today always constructs a new Visit and attaches it to the pet, so it must gain a branch on an optional visitId path variable — the same nullable-path-variable branch PetController.findPet already uses (PetController.java:76). On the correction path it returns the visit the pet already holds, so form binding mutates that instance and owners.save cascades the change in place; the pet's visit set never grows. Resolving that visit needs one by-identity accessor on Pet, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) (Owner.java:126). No new type, no repository, no new pattern, no ADR. Contracts rows for Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController now carry REQ-VIS-003. Basis: direct reads of VisitController.java, PetController.java, Owner.java, Pet.java, Visit.java and createOrUpdateVisitForm.html — the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker (non-symbol-resolved) basis.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit added to VisitController; success redirects to /owners/{ownerId}, as booking does
VisitController's shared @ModelAttribute("visit") loader branches on an optional visitId: existing visit for the correction route, new visit for the booking route
Pet gains a by-identity visit accessor; the visit is reached only through owner -> pet -> visits, never through a repository (system-design.md#contracts, 'Invariants the rows cannot carry')
pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm needs no change: its th:if="${visit['new']}" heading branch and previous-visits table already render the non-new case, and the form posts to the current URL

patterns.description: findPet: shared @ModelAttribute branching on a nullable path variable to serve both the create and the edit route
initUpdateForm/processUpdateForm: twin create/edit route pair on one controller behind one form template
getPet(Integer): by-identity lookup scoped to the aggregate — the shape Pet's visit accessor mirrors
the non-future-date rejection that both routes must share

risks.risk: The shared @ModelAttribute loader adds a fresh Visit to the pet on every request in this controller; left unbranched, opening or submitting the correction form silently gives the pet a second visit
risks.mitigation: Branch before constructing: on the correction route resolve the existing visit and attach nothing. The PRD's third acceptance criterion is the guard (test theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddASecondVisitToThePet asserts the pet's visit count); the invariant is system-design.md#contracts, 'Visit persisted only through cascade from Owner'

risks.risk: Copying the non-future-date block into the correction handler puts a second controller-resident expression of the rule into the code
risks.mitigation: Express it once — a shared private check in VisitController called by both handlers. architecture-principles.md § Pattern catalog (Web controller row, and the note that a new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation not covered by the recorded deviation) admits the existing rule reaching a second entry point, not a new copy. Moving the rule to a VisitValidator is the catalog's preferred destination but is out of this slice's scope, since it would change the booking path

risks.risk: Resolving visitId outside the owner/pet graph would let any caller correct any visit through a mismatched URL
risks.mitigation: Resolve visitId only within the pet already resolved from ownerId, so a visit the pet does not hold is simply not found and is refused the way an unknown petId is refused today. security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries (validate external input at the boundary; grant the minimum scope) and system-design.md#contracts (no VisitRepository exists) both force this

risks.risk: A new handler that omits identifier-binding protection would let the form carry a visit id
risks.mitigation: The controller-wide @InitBinder disallowing id and *.id already covers the new route; keep it unnamed so it applies to every model attribute. security-principles.md § Realization, Mass assignment row

risks.risk: Editing the form template to relabel the submit button pulls in REQ-LANG-002, which requires the key in all eleven bundles
risks.mitigation: Reuse the template unchanged; the narrowest reading of the owner's instruction to reuse pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm needs no markup change

risks.risk: A visit whose date has already passed renders with the date input's min attribute set to tomorrow
risks.mitigation: Treat the min attribute as a client hint only; the server-side future-date check is authoritative, which is what PRD Visits edge case 3 and test thePastDatedVisitCorrectionShouldStillRequireAFutureDate require

notes: Five-signal foundational check: none trips. Architecture shape and stack are recorded in ADRs, system-design.md is populated and partly confirmed, ubiquitous-language.md is written and confirmed, and persistence, validation and error-flow patterns for this concern already exist. The slice introduces no bounded context. Autofix audit: the handoff log holds no design-doc-autofix records, so the audit is a no-op. On the PRD's open question 'what happens when a correction names a visit belonging to a different pet or owner' — the aggregate-scoped lookup this design mandates means such a visitId is never found, and the refusal follows from the existing not-found path rather than from a new product decision. That is a structural consequence, not an answer; the question stays open in docs/prd.md. Cosmetic and uncovered by any requirement: the reused template's previous-visits table lists the visit being corrected alongside the others. Effort rated involved because the model-attribute branch and the in-place update semantics are subtler than the PetController seam they follow.

NG-5 covers only cancellation; deletion of a visit is NG-4's row ('Deleting an owner, a pet, or a visit'). A reader tracing the non-goal citation to verify scope is misdirected to the wrong row for half the sentence.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain: not verified against the NVD in this review. No OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is configured in build.gradle, and the reviewer has no network access, so no CVE match ran — treat the dependency check as not run rather than clean. The change itself adds no supply-chain surface (build.gradle unchanged, no new or upgraded artifact), so this is for CI or a human to close, not a defect in this slice.

Worth extending to name the visit identifier the next time that section is revised, so the next reviewer's first read of the security profile matches the routes.

Defense in depth on the authorization control is tested at the unit level (PetTests.thePetShouldNotFindAVisitItDoesNotHold) but not at the HTTP boundary. A VisitControllerTests case posting a visitId the pet does not hold, asserting the correction is refused and no visit is mutated, would pin the refusal at the layer an attacker actually reaches. Not a defect — the control is present and the two halves are each covered.
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization on the new correction routes is correct and is the security-load-bearing part of the change: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit resolves the visit only inside the pet already resolved from the path owner (VisitController.java:79-98), via the new Pet.getVisit(Integer) (Pet.java:86-96). A visitId belonging to another pet or owner is not found and the request is refused, so there is no IDOR path from /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit to another owner's data.
